content.definition: AHF refers to rapid or gradual onset of symptoms and/or signs of heart failure (HF), severe enough to require urgent medical attention, often leading to unplanned hospital admission or emergency department visit. Patients may require urgent evaluation and initiation or intensification of treatment including intravenous therapies or procedures.
content.epidemiology_and_outcomes: AHF is a leading cause of hospitalizations in subjects aged >65 years and is associated with high mortality and rehospitalization rates. In-hospital mortality ranges from 4% to 10%. Post-discharge 1-year mortality can be 25%–30% with up to more than 45% deaths or readmission rates.
content.clinical_presentation_and_triggers: AHF may be a first manifestation of new-onset HF or due to acute decompensation of chronic HF. Specific extrinsic factors may precipitate but not cause AHF in patients with pre-existing cardiac dysfunction. Clinical severity and in-hospital trajectory are determined by interplay between precipitants, underlying cardiac substrate, and patient comorbidities.
content.diagnostic_workup: Workup starts at first medical contact and continues throughout initial patient pathway to identify clinical presentation and reversible causes/coexisting life-threatening conditions. Diagnostic tests include ECG and echocardiography if possible. Chest X-ray and lung ultrasound may be used to confirm diagnosis, especially when natriuretic peptide testing is not available.
content.natriuretic_peptides_and_cutoffs: Plasma natriuretic peptides (BNP, NT-proBNP, MR-proANP) should be measured if diagnosis is uncertain and a point-of-care assay is available. Normal concentrations make AHF unlikely. Cut-offs for acute HF: BNP <100 pg/mL, NT-proBNP <300 pg/mL, MR-proANP <120 pg/mL. Elevated NP values are associated with a wide range of cardiac and non-cardiac conditions; low concentrations can be detected in advanced end-stage HF, obesity, flash pulmonary oedema or right-sided AHF. Higher levels occur with concomitant atrial fibrillation and/or reduced renal function.
